findings_qualitative.value: First detection of millimeter recombination line emission (H30alpha) toward the Becklin-Neugebauer object

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of mm RL emission toward the BN object.

findings_qualitative.value: The H30alpha line is narrower and redshifted relative to H53alpha, consistent with pressure broadening in H53alpha and optical depth effects in an outflowing ionized envelope

evidence.quote: The H30alpha line is narrower than the H53alpha line, and it is redshifted by a few km s^-1. This behavior has been observed in hypercompact HII regions around embedded young massive stars

findings_qualitative.value: Millimeter continuum variations in BN are possible given historical CARMA non-detection, but multi-epoch observations with uniform setups are required to rule out systematic calibration and uv-coverage differences

evidence.quote: One possible explanation for the differences in the mm fluxes that have been reported for BN is that they are, at least partially, caused by systematic errors in the measurements.

claims.hypothesis: Millimeter recombination line H30alpha traces the systemic line-of-sight velocity of the central star in the BN object better than centimeter lines
claims.experiment: Measure and fit Gaussian line profiles to ALMA H30alpha and VLA H53alpha recombination line spectra toward BN
claims.result: H30alpha has FWHM = 15.4 +- 1.3 km s^-1 and peak velocity v_LSR = 26.3 +- 0.5 km s^-1, narrower than H53alpha (39.0 +- 5.0 km s^-1)
claims.finding: H30alpha is virtually free of pressure broadening and traces the dense, static base of the ionized nebula, giving a systemic velocity v_LSR(BN) = 26.3 +- 0.5 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Therefore, the H30alpha line should give a better estimation of the line-of-sight velocity of the star inside the BN nebula, v_LSR(BN)=26.3+-0.5 km s^-1.

claims.hypothesis: The ionized gas around BN has low bulk motion and moderate electron temperature
claims.experiment: Analyze the narrow linewidth of H30alpha using standard broadening equations (thermal, dynamical, and pressure)
claims.result: The total linewidth is 15.4 km s^-1, which is smaller than thermal width alone for Te = 10^4 K
claims.finding: The electron temperature is Te <= 4900 K, bulk motions are << 10 km s^-1, and average electron density is 8.4 x 10^6 cm^-3

evidence.quote: Therefore, for the gas traced by the H30alpha line, T_e is at most 4900 K, and the bulk gas motions are constrained to be much smaller than the thermal width.

claims.hypothesis: The Becklin-Neugebauer object exhibits millimeter continuum flux variability
claims.experiment: Compare the ALMA 1.3-mm flux density (126 +- 14 mJy) with previous measurements from OVRO (150 +- 50 mJy) and CARMA (< 34 mJy), as well as multi-epoch VLA 3.6-cm fluxes
claims.result: ALMA detects BN at 126 mJy, while CARMA previously reported a non-detection (< 34 mJy), but VLA 3.6-cm flux is stable within 30%
claims.finding: Millimeter continuum variations are possible, though systematic errors in calibration and inhomogeneous uv-coverage could also contribute

evidence.quote: It is possible that BN is variable in the (sub)mm continuum.
We emphasize that only dedicated multiepoch observations with a uniform setup can clarify this issue.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Science Verification data toward Orion BN/KL provide high sensitivity at 1.3 mm covering H30alpha to study recombination lines and continuum

evidence.quote: In this paper we report our findings in the recently released Science Verification (SV) data taken toward Orion BN/KL with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

why_this_method.value: Excluding baselines shorter than 100 klambda filters out confusing extended emission from the hot core to isolate BN

evidence.quote: We found that a minimum baseline length of approx 100 klambda gives optimal results, filtering out the emission on scales >1.4".

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Considered using the full baseline range for imaging BN and H30alpha, but rejected for primary analysis because extended emission and sidelobes from the hot core create contamination

evidence.quote: The H30alpha line is also detected in maps that use the complete baseline range, but bright molecular emission from the HC centered at ~ 10 MHz blueshifted with respect to the RL creates sidelobes that are for the most part removed by taking only the longest baselines.
